narr: Scattered thunderstorms and small storm clusters developed across the North Carolina Piedmont during the evening. Several of these clusters moved over south Charlotte, where multiple storms moved repeatedly over the same locations. Very heavy rainfall and significant flash flooding resulted. One of the storms also produced hail over Charlotte.
ev: Stream gauges and the media reported flash flooding developed across south Charlotte after 2.5 to 5 inches of rain fell across the area due to slow-moving, repeating thunderstorms. Most of the major streams in this part of the city overflowed their banks and inundated adjacent roads, greenways, and residential yards, including Little Hope Creek, Edwards Branch, and Little Sugar Creek. The most significant flooding occurred along Steele Creek in the Steele Creek community, which inundated a mobile home park. Multiple manufactured homes were inundated in this area, and multiple vehicles were largely subsumed in water. Around 30 swift water rescues occurred throughout the city during the event, with most of these occurring in the mobile home park. Thirteen people were also rescued from their vehicles near Freedom Park (Little Sugar Creek). McMullen Creek also experienced severe flooding, with water entering the crawl spaces of some homes and cutting off access to others.
lsr: The stream gauge on McMullen Creek above Lincrest Place exceeded flood stage at around 830 PM. Its still rising and approaching major flood stage as of 930 PM.
A stream gauge on Little Hope Creek at Seneca Place exceeded flood stage at 830 PM. As of 945 PM, the stream had begun to recede.
A stream gauge on Edwards Branch at Sheffield Dr exceeded flood stage at 830 PM and returned to its banks around 920 PM.
A stream gauge on McMullen Creek at Sharon View Rd exceeded flood stage at 840 PM. The stream was beginning to recede at this location as of 940 PM.
The gauge on Little Sugar Creek at Archdale Dr exceeded flood stage at 850 PM. As of 930 PM, the stream is still rising and near moderate flood stage.
A stream gauge on Little Sugar Creek at Hillside Ave exceeded flood stage at 855 PM. The stream was beginning to recede at this location as of 940 PM.
Steele Creek flooded Arrowood Mobile Home park and also flooded Choate Circle downstream. Time approximate.
